name: Sendero Macuco to Salto Arrechea
why: The quiet side of Iguazú: an hour of flat rainforest track away from the catwalk crowds, ending at a waterfall you can stand under.
book: Park ticket at the gate or online (ventaweb.apn.gob.ar); from 1 June 2026 a day pass costs ARS 60,000 for foreigners. The trail starts near the Estación Central of the jungle train and closes at 15:00. Buses run from Puerto Iguazú to the park gate.
water: Carry 1-2 litres: no water or food on the trail; buy it at the park centre.
dangers: Heat and humidity: start in the morning and carry water.
The last stretch down to the falls is steep, wet and slippery.
Coatis and monkeys: keep food closed and don't feed them.
turnaround: The trail closes at 15:00: start by 12:00 to walk it calmly.

points.name: Sendero Macuco trailhead
points.note: Near the Estación Central of the jungle train. The first hour is a flat dirt track under the forest canopy; capuchin monkeys and toucans are common.

points.name: Salto Arrechea
points.note: A steep path and stairs drop to the pool under the 20 m fall; you can swim when it is calm. Return the same way.
